title: Unit – 4 : Session – 12 : SLO – 2  |  Evaluate and Document the Paradigm Usage
sections: In my project (a task-tracker web app), the entire data-transformation layer is written in the functional paradigm: every update is a pure function that maps the current task list to a new one instead of mutating shared state.
Filtering completed tasks, sorting by deadline and computing statistics are composed using map(), filter() and reduce() with lambda expressions, so each operation is independently testable.
Because the functions are side-effect free, the UI simply re-renders from the returned state — demonstrating referential transparency and making the code easier to debug and extend.
